_meta.title: Application review rubric — accumulated lessons the adversarial reviewer enforces
_meta.purpose: The hostile internal reviewer tears every grant/patent/proposal apart against these BEFORE it reaches the operator. Each lesson = a known failure mode learned from real reviewer/NSF feedback. To LEARN + EXPAND: add a lesson (one entry) whenever feedback reveals a new failure mode. lane: 'all' or pipe-list e.g. 'grant|research'.
_meta.source: Session learnings 2026-06-06 + NSF SBIR reviewer feedback patterns

lessons.check: Any performance metric or result presented as 'validated'/'proven' that is not clearly reproducible and documented. In a federal filing this is false-statement exposure and the first thing a reviewer attacks.
lessons.fix: Only include reproducible, documented results. Otherwise frame as 'preliminary internal analysis suggests' and never overstate. Strip any number you cannot defend.

lessons.check: The deep-tech innovation (the core technology/kernel) is buried under an application-layer product, so it reads as a vertical startup rather than fundable deep tech ('is this just an HR-tech/fintech app?').
lessons.fix: Lead with the core technology as the technical innovation; position the application as the Phase I validation; give Phase II a multi-vertical expansion path.

lessons.check: Objectives requiring multi-site controlled intervention, an RCT, or human-subjects OUTCOME measurement — that is Phase II scope, not Phase I feasibility. IRB + recruitment alone eats 3-6 months.
lessons.fix: Drop outcome-measurement objectives to Phase II. Reframe Phase I as 'design + pilot-feasibility test' only. Keep objectives to detection/validation of the core claim.

lessons.check: Solo founder / single-member LLC, no named co-PI/advisor, no named IRB, only 'planned/hypothetical' hires, no prior award. Reviewers doubt one person can execute a 6-12 month Phase I and ask who peer-reviews methodology.
lessons.fix: Name >=1 credentialed advisor; name the commercial IRB with a letter of intent; specify hires with criteria and named candidates if possible; state PI effort (>=173 hrs / 6 months) and how it's met given other commitments.

lessons.check: For an AI/ML-topic submission, the technical innovation is described in domain/narrative terms (neuroscience, behavior) without the computational specifics. Pure-ML reviewers can't evaluate it.
lessons.fix: Keep the domain framing as MOTIVATION; make the Technical Innovation section explicit about the computational architecture, algorithmic class, and how it differs from existing change-point, anomaly-detection, and sequence-prediction methods.

lessons.check: Widely-cited but contested statistics (e.g., '60-70% of change initiatives fail/revert in 18 months') used without a primary, defensible citation. Some reviewers know the stat's provenance is weak.
lessons.fix: Cite a primary peer-reviewed source or rephrase to a specific defensible claim. For change-failure, anchor to the McKinsey 2008/2015 transformation studies and avoid the harder-to-source 'reversion within 18 months' specificity.

lessons.check: Wrong funder template: NIH structure/ceiling on an NSF submission (or vice versa); wrong applicant type (501(c)(3) for SBIR which requires a small business); cost-share included where NSF prohibits it.
lessons.fix: Match the template to the actual funder/program. SBIR applicant = the LLC (small business). NSF: no cost-share, 10% de minimis, Project Summary 3 headers, 15-page Project Description, Commercialization Plan. Confirm the current ceiling.

lessons.check: No explicit, pre-registered falsification criterion — reviewers can't tell what a clean negative result looks like.
lessons.fix: State a pre-registered success/failure threshold (e.g., 'events must cluster around identified cues with measurable lead time; if not, the model fails, reported transparently').

lessons.check: GATE 1. Any named entity, citation, PA/solicitation number, grant track, recall number, or company segment that may be fabricated or unverifiable (e.g., fake FDA recall 'Z-0611-2022', defunct DARPA program, mis-cited paper, wrong author/year). One web search can falsify these.
lessons.fix: Verify every named entity, citation, PA/track number, and segment name against an authoritative source before the card propagates. Flag anything unverifiable and exclude it.

lessons.check: GATE 2. The card commits to a 'pathology' reading without first ruling out the rational, non-pathological explanation (option-value preservation, normal procurement gaps, lender covenants, price-driven capital discipline, legitimate utilization management).
lessons.fix: Require one paragraph that rules out the rational non-pathological explanation before committing to the pathology reading.

lessons.check: GATE 3. Core indicators are not computable on the current stack (SEC EDGAR, FRED, BLS, EIA, Treasury, USASpending, Form 4/13F). Off-stack dependencies (IQVIA, Symphony, Definitive Healthcare, company-internal telemetry like LibreView) are treated as if available.
lessons.fix: Label each indicator computable / non-computable. Non-computable core signals must get a data-feed plan (or grant-funded data access) or be cut. Don't score a lane on data you can't get.

lessons.check: Card applied to a company purely by SIC code without checking the company actually still fits (the AGIG/Abundia failure, 7+ occurrences: a Colombia-focused/renewables-pivoting micro-cap scored as a US federal-acreage E&P).
lessons.fix: Before applying, verify the latest 10-K business description + EDGAR name-change events (24mo) + recent M&A/restructuring. If the named target has pivoted, RETARGET to a universe match (stable operators that actually fit the pathology) instead of the stale SIC instance.

lessons.check: Company facts phrased as 'portal notes document…' / 'portal signals indicate…' rather than traced to a primary source — risk of LLM-confabulated specifics propagating into indicator scores (e.g., implausible 'JPMorgan/BofA/Wells are the revolver lenders' for a micro-cap).
lessons.fix: Every company fact must trace to a specific 10-K section, XBRL fact, or USASpending record. Facts without primary-source provenance are flagged 'unverified' and excluded from indicator scoring.

lessons.check: Multiple cards generated at the same/adjacent neural substrate for the same business pathology (PPN vs PPTN = same nucleus; lPFC vs dlPFC adjacent), inflating apparent coverage.
lessons.fix: Collapse neural-region synonyms via a controlled vocabulary; before approving a new card, check whether an existing card at the same substrate diagnoses the same pathology and require an explicit neurally-distinct articulation.

lessons.check: Wrong entity/segment names or SIC codes (e.g., 'Abbott Metabolic' — not a real segment; it's Abbott Diabetes Care within Medical Devices; CGM mis-coded SIC 3842). Recurs 12+ times — signals a portal-notes metadata error.
lessons.fix: Use exact, verified entity/segment names and correct SIC codes; a wrong name is a flag to reconcile the whole portal note against primary filings.
